business.name: Dallas Power Washing Pro
business.dba_note: Dallas Power Washing Pro is a d/b/a of Dominion Digital Group.
business.category: Free pressure washing and soft washing referral phone line for Dallas-Fort Worth
business.hours_text: The phone line is answered 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by an automated assistant.
business.description: Dallas Power Washing Pro is a free phone line for homeowners and businesses across Dallas-Fort Worth. An automated assistant answers any hour, asks what needs cleaning, and puts the call through to an independent, locally owned pressure washing company that inspects, quotes, does the work and is paid by the customer directly.
business.short_disclosure: Dallas Power Washing Pro is a free phone line, not a pressure washing company. It answers your call and connects you with an independent local pressure washing company, which inspects, quotes and does the work, and which you pay directly.
business.referral_disclosure: Companies may pay a referral fee. Callers never pay the line.
business.other_lines: The same number also takes AC and heating, roofing, water damage and mold calls for the Dallas area, so the assistant first asks what you need.
business.quote_text: I believe the unbelievable, I receive the impossible, because it's doable.

services.name: Residential Pressure Washing
services.card_alt: Worker pressure washing a concrete driveway in front of a brick house
services.summary: Patios, walks, pool decks, porches and the rest of the hard surfaces around a DFW home, matched with a company that sets the pressure to the surface.

services.name: House Washing and Soft Washing
services.card_alt: Man soft washing the brick and siding of a two-story house
services.summary: Brick, stone, stucco, fiber cement and vinyl washed with low pressure and a cleaning solution, so green film comes off without forcing water behind the wall.

services.name: Roof Cleaning and Roof Soft Washing
services.card_alt: Roof half cleaned, showing the difference between stained and clean tiles
services.summary: Black streaks on shingles are usually algae. The shingle makers say never blast them, so the call goes to a company that soft washes roofs.

services.name: Driveway and Concrete Cleaning
services.card_alt: Freshly cleaned concrete driveway and walk in front of a brick home with a white garage door
services.summary: Tire marks, oil drips, rust fans and the gray film on shaded concrete, cleaned evenly with a surface cleaner instead of striped with a wand.

services.name: Commercial Power Washing
services.card_alt: Worker pressure washing a sidewalk in front of a row of storefronts
services.summary: Storefront walks, drive-thru lanes, dumpster pads and parking areas, washed by a company that knows the city's rules on where the dirty water goes.

services.name: Fence Cleaning
services.card_alt: Weathered wood privacy fence being cleaned with a spray wand
services.summary: Gray, mildewed wood privacy fences brought back with a gentle wash, ready for stain, without tearing up the grain.

services.name: Deck and Patio Cleaning
services.card_alt: Weathered wood deck with patio furniture in the evening sun
services.summary: Wood and composite decks, covered patios and pergolas cleaned the way the decking maker allows, so the warranty and the boards survive.

cities.name: Fort Worth
cities.summary: The city that permits mobile power washers and bans wash water in the storm drain, from the Stockyards to the historic districts.

cities.name: Arlington
cities.summary: Between Dallas and Fort Worth, with stadium-district businesses, campus rentals and a drinking water lake inside the city.

cities.name: Plano
cities.summary: Neighborhoods built in the 1970s to 1990s boom, a twice-a-week watering schedule and a busy corporate side along Legacy.

cities.name: Frisco
cities.summary: One of the fastest-growing cities in the country, so most neighborhoods were built after 2000 and many homes are on their first roof and fence.

cities.name: McKinney
cities.summary: The county seat, with a historic downtown where exterior changes go through review and brand-new subdivisions on the edges.

cities.name: Allen
cities.summary: A former railroad stop that grew from under 2,000 people in 1970 to more than 100,000, with a historic depot, newer subdivisions and busy retail centers.

cities.name: Denton
cities.summary: Two universities, the Courthouse Square and storm drains that run to Lewisville Lake, a drinking water source for much of DFW.

cities.name: Irving
cities.summary: Las Colinas office towers and canal walks on one side, older East Irving neighborhoods on the other.

cities.name: Carrollton
cities.summary: A three-county city with Koreatown storefronts along Old Denton Road and DART stations in its old downtown.

cities.name: Addison
cities.summary: A small town packed with restaurants, patios and apartments, which buys its water from Dallas.

cities.name: Flower Mound
cities.summary: A town beside Grapevine Lake with Cross Timbers trees, larger lots and a staged water plan to check before washing.
